questions.q: Which three building blocks does the introductory lecture say shape tourism practices in local history work?
options: Historical identity, collective memory and cultural resources
questions.explain: Topic 1: the lecture explores the role of historical identity, collective memory and cultural resources in shaping tourism practices.

questions.q: Which three things does Topic 2 study to understand the heritage tourist?
questions.explain: Topic 2 examines visitor motivations, demographic patterns and psychological drivers that distinguish heritage tourists from other travelers.

questions.q: Which criteria are used in Topic 3 to evaluate heritage resources for tourism? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explain: Topic 3: resources are evaluated for integrity, significance and authenticity (the seminar also adds accessibility).

questions.q: In Topic 5, which group of stakeholders is named as needing coordination in a heritage tourism strategy?
questions.explain: Topic 5: strategic planning includes stakeholder coordination between hotels, museums and municipalities.

questions.q: What is the central tension in sustainable site management (Topic 6)?
questions.explain: Topic 6: conservation priority (minimise wear, protect microclimates) conflicts with visitation priority (education, maintenance revenue).

questions.q: Which level of Tourism Carrying Capacity (TCC) means the limit of crowding for visitor appreciation and resident comfort?
questions.explain: Topic 6: social capacity is the limit of crowding for visitor appreciation and resident comfort. Physical = spatial density; ecological = reversible degradation threshold.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the four steps of the Limits of Acceptable Change (LAC) framework?
options: Take action → Set indicators → Define values → Fix standards
Define values → Set indicators → Fix standards → Take action
Fix standards → Define values → Take action → Set indicators
Set indicators → Take action → Define values → Fix standards
questions.explain: Topic 6: Define values (core assets) → Set indicators (abrasion, humidity) → Fix standards (critical limits) → Take action (entry caps, routing).

questions.q: Which tools belong to the visitor flow management toolkit in Topic 6? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Unlimited free entry at peak hours
questions.explain: Topic 6: timed entry (hourly quotas), dynamic pricing (peak-hour adjustments) and micro-zoning (core vs. buffer zones).

questions.q: Which Venice Charter principles are listed in Topic 6 for maintaining authenticity?
options: Full reconstruction of lost buildings in modern materials
Removing later layers to show only the oldest one
Minimal physical intervention and preservation of all historical layers
Replacing originals with copies for visitor safety
questions.explain: Topic 6: the Venice Charter principles are minimal physical site intervention and preservation of all historical layers; modern interpretation avoids false reconstruction.

questions.q: According to Topic 6, sustainability at a heritage site is a static state that is reached once and then kept.
questions.explain: The lecture recap says sustainability is a continuous adaptive process, not a static state.

questions.q: Which technology is used for predictive modelling of structural strain and wear at heritage sites?
questions.explain: Topic 6: BIM digital twins predict structural strain and wear; heatmaps track crowd bottlenecks; IoT sensors track humidity and vibration.

questions.q: Complete Tilden's principle: "Through interpretation, understanding; through understanding, appreciation; through appreciation, ..."
questions.explain: Topic 7: Tilden's chain ends with protection – interpretation leads to understanding, appreciation and finally protection.

questions.q: Which are the three pillars of authentic heritage storytelling (Topic 7)? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explain: Topic 7: human connection, universal themes and a provocative arc that raises questions instead of giving dry encyclopedic answers.

questions.q: In the eco-museum approach, local residents act as primary narrators and custodians of heritage.
questions.explain: Topic 7: the eco-museum is based on community ownership, territory over trophy cases and intangible traditions.

questions.q: Which techniques does Topic 7 recommend for children and families?
options: Gamification, treasure quests and character-driven roleplay
questions.explain: Topic 7: children and families – gamification, quests, roleplay; seniors – comfortable pace, clear acoustics, rest points; international guests – visual symbols, multilingual apps.

questions.q: The first step of designing an interpretive plan is visitor evaluation.
questions.explain: Topic 7: the steps are 1) asset audit, 2) theme framing, 3) medium selection, 4) visitor evaluation. Evaluation is the last step.
